title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed, mimeographed Bourbaki draft (header 'n° 392', '4 - 22 -') bound upside down among the handwritten L-function notes, probably reused as scrap paper. Its content matches Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative, ch. VII 'Diviseurs', §4 (modules over Krull domains, pseudo-isomorphisms), around n° 5.

Setting: A is a Krull domain and P is its set of height-one primes. For a finitely generated torsion A-module T, the divisor is χ(T) = Σ_{p∈P} ℓ_{A_p}(T_p)·p, an element of the divisor group D(A) (Déf. 4).

Proposition 10 states:
(i) χ is additive on short exact sequences. This follows because localization is exact (ch. II §2 n°4 th. 1) and length is additive.
(ii) A pseudo-isomorphism T1→T2 gives χ(T1) = χ(T2), since kernel and cokernel have no support at height-one primes.
(iii) χ(T) = 0 if and only if T is pseudo-null.

The corollary gives the alternating-sum formula for a finite exact sequence.

The page then defines T(A) ⊂ F(A), the isomorphism classes of finitely generated torsion modules, and begins Proposition 11. This is the universal property: an additive function φ on T(A) into an abelian group G, presumably satisfying a second condition (vanishing on pseudo-null modules or on A/p-type modules), factors uniquely through χ. The page stops after condition 1).

The connection to Grothendieck's surrounding notes is at best incidental. Those notes concern ε- and δ-constants in the functional equation of L-functions of ℓ-adic sheaves. Both settings involve additive invariants, but there is no evidence the sheet was chosen for its content.
errors: None mathematically; standard and correct. The statement of Prop. 11 is cut off at condition 1).

ideas.what: Divisor χ(T) of a finitely generated torsion module over a Krull domain: additivity, invariance under pseudo-isomorphism, vanishing exactly on pseudo-null modules
ideas.modern_name: Divisor / characteristic ideal of a torsion module over a Krull domain (structure theory up to pseudo-isomorphism, as used in Iwasawa theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bourbaki (Algèbre commutative ch. VII, 1965); background from Krull, Serre's Iwasawa-module structure theory

ideas.what: Universal property of χ among additive functions on classes of torsion modules (Prop. 11)
ideas.modern_name: χ as universal additive invariant: K-theoretic description of the divisor group modulo pseudo-null modules

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a published Bourbaki draft on divisors of torsion modules over Krull domains, apparently reused as scrap paper. It contains no original Grothendieck content.
